description: Eval cases for the agent routing matrix skill. Each case tests whether the agent correctly routes tasks to Cursor (gather), Codex (implement), or Claude (orchestrate). All cases derive from real violations in April 4, 2026 orcClaude session.

effort_routing_gate.grader_instruction: For eval IDs 24-32, score the selected effort against expected_effort. At least 8 of 9 exact tiers must match. Also check that the answer explains its model choice, makes -E explicit when repoGolem can carry the choice, and reports effective model plus effort from the run's own turn_context; for a child, use the turn_context after the child's own task_started.

evals.prompt: I need to understand what's in the BrainLayer SQLite database -- how many chunks, what tags exist, whether the FTS5 index is in sync. Can you run some queries to check?
evals.expected_output: Should route this to a Cursor worker via cmux, NOT run sqlite3 queries itself. This is a read-only data-gathering task.

assertions.text: Routes the SQL querying task to a Cursor worker (mentions spawning Cursor, cmux, or delegating the queries)
Does NOT run sqlite3 or SQL queries directly itself
Includes READ-ONLY instruction in the Cursor prompt (no modifications to the database)
Specifies an output location for Cursor's findings (e.g., docs.local/ or a findings file)

evals.prompt: The FTS5 index is 96% out of sync. We need to rebuild it -- can you write a migration script that drops and recreates the FTS5 triggers?
evals.expected_output: Should route this implementation task to Codex, NOT write the migration script itself. This is a code change task.

assertions.text: Routes the implementation task to Codex (mentions spawning Codex, delegating the code work)
Does NOT write the migration script itself using Write/Edit tools
Provides Codex with clear requirements for the migration (what to drop, what to recreate)
Does NOT route this implementation work to Cursor (Cursor is read-only)

evals.prompt: We're starting a new sprint collab. brainClaude will investigate BrainLayer search quality issues, and we need code fixes applied. Write the collab kickoff.
evals.expected_output: The collab kickoff MUST include an Agent Routing section that assigns Cursor for investigation/data-gathering, Codex for code fixes, and Claude for coordination.

assertions.text: Includes an Agent Routing table or section in the collab
Assigns data-gathering/investigation tasks to Cursor (not Claude)
Assigns code fix/implementation tasks to Codex (not Claude or Cursor)
Assigns coordination/review tasks to Claude
Does NOT assign implementation work directly to the Claude agent

evals.prompt: I'm checking on the sprint agents. brainClaude is at 72% context and has been running sqlite3 queries for the last 20 minutes. The Cursor worker on surface:63 was spawned but has 0 tokens -- it never received a task. What should I do?
evals.expected_output: Should flag this as a routing violation. brainClaude is doing Cursor work itself. Should nudge brainClaude to delegate remaining queries to the Cursor worker, and verify the Cursor surface is still alive.

assertions.text: Identifies the situation as a routing violation (Claude doing Cursor work)
Recommends sending remaining query work to the idle Cursor worker
Checks whether the Cursor surface is still alive (list_surfaces or read_screen)
Does NOT accept the situation as normal or say 'brainClaude is handling it fine'
Notes that 72% context burn on data gathering is wasteful when a Cursor worker exists

evals.prompt: We need to audit all 53 skill files in golem-powers/ to check which ones have evals and which don't. Then for any skills missing evals, we need to create eval cases. How should we set this up?
evals.expected_output: Should split into two phases: (1) Cursor scans all skill directories for evals (read-only audit), (2) Codex creates missing eval files (implementation). Claude coordinates and reviews.

assertions.text: Splits the task into a gathering phase (audit) and implementation phase (create evals)
Routes the audit/scan phase to Cursor (read-only file listing and checking)
Routes the eval creation phase to Codex (file creation is implementation)
Does NOT try to do both the scan and the creation in a single agent
Mentions an intermediate output (e.g., findings file) that bridges the two phases

evals.prompt: The Cursor worker on surface:68 seems to have crashed -- it's not responding to read_screen. The Claude agent hasn't noticed and is still waiting for results. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Should immediately respawn the Cursor worker on a new surface, resend the original task, and notify the Claude agent. Don't wait for the Claude to discover the crash on its own.

assertions.text: Takes immediate action to respawn the crashed Cursor worker
Creates a NEW surface for the respawned worker (not reusing the crashed one)
Resends the original task to the new Cursor worker
Notifies the Claude agent about the respawn and new surface reference
Does NOT tell the Claude agent to 'just do the Cursor work itself'

evals.prompt: I need to scan all Python files in ~/Gits/brainlayer/ for any function that has a docstring but no implementation body (stubs). Can you grep for that pattern?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this as a read-only data-gathering task and route to Cursor. Should NOT run grep itself, as this is mechanical file scanning that burns Claude context.

assertions.text: Routes the grep/scanning task to a Cursor worker
Does NOT run grep or file scanning commands directly itself
Provides the Cursor worker with the specific grep pattern or search criteria
Specifies where Cursor should write results (docs.local/ or similar)

evals.prompt: brainClaude just finished its sprint. Looking at the collab log, it did all 5 SQL queries itself, never sent anything to its Cursor worker, and also wrote a 200-line fix directly instead of using Codex. How do we prevent this next time?
evals.expected_output: Should identify two violations: (1) SQL queries should have gone to Cursor, (2) 200-line fix should have gone to Codex. Should recommend adding routing verification gates to future collabs.

assertions.text: Identifies the SQL queries as a routing violation (should be Cursor)
Identifies the 200-line implementation as a routing violation (should be Codex)
Recommends specific process improvements (routing verification gates, utilization checks)
Does NOT dismiss the violations as 'it got the job done anyway'
References the routing matrix (Cursor=gather, Codex=implement, Claude=orchestrate)

evals.prompt: Choose the Codex launcher/model for these two jobs: (A) a single-file review of a 180-line patch that I can describe in two sentences, and (B) a multi-file refactor that will touch 7 files, needs a collab file, and will probably land around 900 LOC. Also tell me whether GPT-5.4-mini should be the default fast path.
evals.expected_output: Should route both (A) and (B) through `brainlayerCodex -s`; (A) should NOT be sent through a shortcut fast flag or automatic Spark routing. If Spark is mentioned at all, it must be framed only as an explicit `-m gpt-5.3-codex-spark` override for cases where the dispatcher intentionally asks for that model. GPT-5.4-mini must be rejected as the routine default for Codex work.

assertions.text: Routes the single-file 180-line review through `brainlayerCodex -s`
Routes the 7-file collab-backed 900 LOC refactor to the main-pool default via `-s` alone (no `-m` flag)
Frames Spark only as an explicit `-m gpt-5.3-codex-spark` override if it is mentioned
Rejects GPT-5.4-mini as the routine default path for Codex work
Does NOT recommend `--fast`
Does NOT automatically route the small task to Spark unless the prompt explicitly asks for Spark

evals.prompt: I need to spawn a Cursor worker in the brainlayer repo to audit FTS5 sync. Give me the exact one-liner to dispatch it.
evals.expected_output: Should output exactly `brainlayerCursor -s "..."` (the prompt content can vary). Should NOT include `cd ~/Gits/brainlayer`, `MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING=1`, `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1`, `source ~/.zshrc &&`, or a raw `cursor agent` invocation. This is the AP11 test (2026-05-21 severity-10 mandate).

assertions.text: Uses the `brainlayerCursor -s` launcher form (matches regex `^brainlayerCursor -s `)
Does NOT include `cd ~/Gits/` or any `cd` before the launcher
Does NOT include `MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING=1` (launcher exports this)
Does NOT include `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1` (launcher exports this)
Does NOT include `source ~/.zshrc` (launcher is already in the calling shell)
Does NOT call raw `cursor agent` or `cursor` directly (skips launcher infrastructure)

evals.prompt: Dispatch a Codex worker to fix a small typo in the brainlayer search.py file. What's the exact command?
evals.expected_output: Should be `brainlayerCodex -s "..."`. Should NOT use `--fast`, should NOT use raw `codex`, should NOT include `cd` or env-var ceremony. The `-s` flag alone is sufficient — it maps to `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` for Codex.

assertions.text: Uses `brainlayerCodex -s` (matches regex `^brainlayerCodex -s `)
Does NOT use the `--fast` flag
Does NOT use raw `codex` (no launcher) or `codex --full-auto`
Does NOT prepend `cd ~/Gits/brainlayer &&`
Does NOT include `MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING=1` or `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1`

evals.prompt: Someone wrote in a collab kickoff: `cd ~/Gits/brainlayer && MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING=1 CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1 cursor agent "audit X"`. Is this correct? If not, what's the fix?
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as an AP11 violation (verbose launcher invocation). Should rewrite it as `brainlayerCursor -s "audit X"`. Should explain that the launcher already does cd + env-var exports + iTerm profile + MCP wiring, so the ceremony is redundant.

assertions.text: Identifies the command as a violation (AP11 or 'verbose launcher invocation' or 'wrong form')
Provides the corrected form using `brainlayerCursor -s`
Explains that the launcher already handles cd, env vars, and infrastructure
Does NOT defend or accept the verbose form as 'also OK' or 'equivalent'

evals.expected_output: Should flag the first two transcript lines as AP11 violations and leave the third line alone. The replacements should be `brainlayerCursor -s "audit read path"` and `brainlayerCodex -s "fix typo"`. The answer should explain that the launcher handles cwd/env/MCP setup and that `--fast` is not a repoGolem routing flag.

assertions.text: Flags the verbose `cd ... MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING=1 CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1 cursor agent` line as an AP11 violation
Flags `brainlayerCodex --fast` as a violation
Provides `brainlayerCursor -s "audit read path"` as the corrected command
Provides `brainlayerCodex -s "fix typo"` as the corrected command
Does NOT flag the existing `brainlayerCursor -s` line as a violation

evals.prompt:
Classify these two dispatches under AP11:

A. Visible cmux pane worker: `cmux send --surface surface:3 "brainlayerCodex --fast \"small implementation\""`
B. Internal ephemeral subagent spawned from inside an agent session: `spawn_agent({"agent_type":"worker", "model":"gpt-5.3-codex-spark", "message":"small implementation"})`

Which one is allowed, and what should A be rewritten to?
evals.expected_output: Should reject A because visible cmux pane workers must use `{repo}{Tool} -s "prompt"` only and must never use `--fast`. Should rewrite A as `brainlayerCodex -s "small implementation"`. Should allow B because it is an internal ephemeral subagent, where Spark is permitted through explicit model selection (`gpt-5.3-codex-spark` or `-m gpt-5.3-codex-spark`). Should state that `--fast` is banned as an alias in both layers.

assertions.text: Identifies A as a visible cmux pane worker dispatch
Rejects `brainlayerCodex --fast` for visible cmux pane workers
Rewrites A to `brainlayerCodex -s "small implementation"`
Identifies B as an internal ephemeral subagent rather than a cmux pane worker
Allows Spark for B through explicit model selection (`gpt-5.3-codex-spark` or `-m gpt-5.3-codex-spark`)
Does NOT allow `--fast` as an alias in either layer

Does NOT spawn a duplicate BrainLayerCodex for the same lane just to get a cleaner prompt
Writes a file-backed goal with the full BrainLayer baseline/cleanup mission
Sends one `/goal Read and execute this goal file until complete: <path>` style prompt to the existing agent_id
States that the stale #554 task is superseded, not forked into a second lane

The lead wants to send a Codex worker only the next narrow PR blocker. Is that acceptable?

Treats the verified DONE marker as the worker completion signal for the lane

Stops high-frequency pane polling or large scrollback reads after file completion is verified

Says merged PRs and CI green are insufficient for BrainLayer baseline greenlight
Requires durable queue state and deferred-store replay verification

Does NOT greenlight Rust planning from dashboard 100% alone

Requires verified report path plus exact DONE marker for done lanes
Allows BLOCKED/NOT_GREEN only with file-backed handoff, health evidence, next action, and owner

Does NOT treat a clean/empty workspace alone as proof of completion

evals.prompt: A Codex worker was assigned an approved production-readiness lane. It finished implementation, tests pass, but now says: 'I cannot commit or merge because the rules say I need explicit permission. Also the BrainLayer MCP needs a restart and Codex cannot reconnect, so I am waiting for Etan.' What does agent-routing require?
evals.expected_output: Should reject permission parking. Approved delegated work authorizes the normal PR loop and in-scope MCP/service recovery. Handles Codex MCP reconnect limits by checkpointing and spawning/resuming a managed successor
Requires post-restart/post-merge real verification before claiming green

Names the narrow class of true human blockers: irreversible data loss, force-push/history rewrite, destructive cleanup of unowned work, credential/account changes, paid external actions, or human-only license/ToS acceptance
Does NOT leave the worker idle waiting for Etan on recoverable blockers

Routes the multi-file refactor to a visible Codex-implements + Claude-reviews pair
Does NOT accept urgency alone as qualifying for the tiny-unblocker carve-out
Does NOT allow shared-tree edits under the tiny-unblocker carve-out

evals.description: A tiny known-output mechanical transformation uses Luna medium; Luna low remains banned.
evals.prompt: Choose a Codex model and effort for this mission: reformat one existing Markdown file to an exact canonical output that has already been supplied. There are no semantic edits or design choices, the answer shape is known byte-for-byte, a deterministic formatter check verifies it, and rollback is one file. State the dispatch approach and what the run's own turn_context must prove.
evals.expected_output: Select Luna at medium for the direct mechanical edit because the output is known and deterministic. Explicitly reject Luna low because it is banned. Pass the outcome plus formatter check and verify the effective model and effort from the run's own turn_context.

assertions.name: selects-luna-medium
assertions.description: Selects Luna medium for the tiny known-output mechanical transformation.
assertions.text: Selects Luna medium

assertions.name: bans-luna-low
assertions.description: Explicitly rejects Luna low.
assertions.text: Bans Luna low

assertions.name: outcome-plus-test
assertions.description: Provides the exact outcome and deterministic formatter check.
assertions.text: Provides outcome plus deterministic test

assertions.name: reports-effective-routing
assertions.description: Requires the effective model and effort from the child's session JSONL turn_context.
assertions.text: Reports effective model and effort from child turn_context

evals.name: omitted-effort-is-silent-choice
evals.description: A dispatch that omits -E must be treated as silently choosing the launcher default rather than making no effort decision.
evals.prompt: Review this draft dispatch for a well-specified bounded implementation lane: `golemsCodex -s "apply the specified adapter patch and run the focused regression test"`. The diff shape is known, the task still requires implementation, and the draft gives no effort choice or rationale. Should it ship unchanged? State the corrected dispatch and explain what the omission means.
evals.expected_output: Reject the draft unchanged. Omitting -E silently accepts an inherited value; it is not the absence of a decision. Require a mission-specific rationale and correct the default Sol implementation dispatch to -E medium, then verify effective model and effort from the run's own turn_context.

assertions.name: flags-omitted-effort
assertions.description: Flags the missing -E as a defect rather than accepting the inherited default.
assertions.text: Flags the omitted -E

assertions.name: calls-silence-a-choice
assertions.description: States that inheriting the default is a decision made silently.
assertions.text: Calls the silent default a choice

assertions.name: requires-mission-rationale
assertions.description: Requires the brief to name an effort and explain why it fits the mission.
assertions.text: Requires an effort rationale

assertions.name: corrects-to-medium
assertions.description: Corrects the bounded implementation dispatch to use -E medium explicitly.
assertions.text: Uses -E medium

evals.name: recon-child-requires-named-agent
evals.description: Open-ended read-heavy Codex child recon uses the named Sol high recon agent.
evals.prompt: A Sol implementation lane needs a child to inspect 30 source files, make no edits, and return a distilled evidence table. Should the parent spawn an unnamed child or a named custom agent? State the target model and effort and the proof required after spawning.
evals.expected_output: Target Sol high for the named recon agent because inspecting and distilling 30 source files is open-ended. Do not use an unnamed child because its inherited model is not a reliable routing choice. The external recon agent may still pin Terra, so verify the child's effective model and effort from the turn_context after its own task_started and correct any mismatch before relying on its output.

assertions.name: uses-named-recon
assertions.description: Requires the named recon custom agent for read-heavy child work.
assertions.text: Uses the named recon agent

assertions.name: selects-sol-high
assertions.description: Targets Sol high for open-ended recon.
assertions.text: Targets gpt-6-sol at high

assertions.name: rejects-unnamed-recon
assertions.description: Does not use the unnamed Luna packet default for recon.
assertions.text: Does not spawn recon as an unnamed child

assertions.name: verifies-child-context
assertions.description: Checks the child turn_context after its own task_started.
assertions.text: Verifies turn_context after child task_started

evals.name: worker-requests-missing-pair-reviewer
evals.description: A Codex implementer without a reviewer pane must ask its lead instead of creating or substituting a reviewer.
evals.prompt: You are a Codex worker in a cmux pane, in a git worktree of the golems repo. Your lead's brief said: add a --json flag to scripts/check-skill-library.mjs, and iterate with your pair-reviewer until both of you are happy, then open the PR. You have finished the diff and your tests pass. No reviewer pane exists and no reviewer agent has contacted you. Do not ask me what the task is; the task is done. State exactly what you do next, as a short numbered list of concrete actions or commands.
evals.expected_output: Ask the lead to open or route the Claude pair-reviewer, then wait for that reviewer. Do not run `claude -p`, spawn a reviewer subagent, self-review, or proceed as though pair review happened.

assertions.name: asks-lead-for-reviewer
assertions.description: Explicitly asks the lead to open or route the missing Claude pair-reviewer.
assertions.text: Asks the lead for the missing reviewer pane

assertions.name: does-not-self-start-reviewer
assertions.description: Does not run claude -p or spawn any reviewer subagent for its own work.
assertions.text: Does NOT start a reviewer of any kind

assertions.name: does-not-substitute-self-review
assertions.description: Does not self-review and proceed without the routed pair-reviewer.
assertions.text: Does NOT self-review and proceed

evals.name: lead-opens-implementation-pair
evals.description: A lead receiving implementation work must create both halves of the pre-PR pair.
evals.prompt: Etan asks for a --json flag on scripts/check-skill-library.mjs. You are the lead for the golems repo and have no panes open. State exactly what you do next, as a short numbered list of concrete actions or commands.
evals.expected_output: Open both panes: a Codex implementer and a Claude pair-reviewer. Keep the reviewer lead-routed, have the pair iterate until both are happy, and only then let Codex open the PR and run `/pr-loop`.

assertions.name: opens-codex-implementer
assertions.description: Opens a Codex implementer pane for the implementation.
assertions.text: Opens the Codex implementer pane

assertions.name: opens-claude-pair-reviewer
assertions.description: Opens a separate Claude pair-reviewer pane for the same work.
assertions.text: Opens the Claude pair-reviewer pane

assertions.name: pair-review-precedes-pr-loop
assertions.description: Keeps pair review before Codex opens the PR and runs pr-loop.
assertions.text: Pair review completes before /pr-loop

evals.name: large-plan-review-owner-pointer-chain
evals.description: Large-plan must point phase completion through pr-loop, which points pre-PR review ownership to agent-routing. Requires agent-routing, large-plan and pr-loop SKILL.md in context; not answerable from agent-routing alone.
evals.prompt: Where does `/large-plan` say who reviews a bounded implementation phase? Follow the owning references and name the source of truth.
evals.expected_output: `/large-plan` only says that a bounded implementation phase ends in `/pr-loop`. `/pr-loop` points pre-PR reviewer identity and pane ownership to `/agent-routing` § Review routing, which is the source of truth; large-plan does not restate the routing rule.

assertions.name: follows-large-plan-to-pr-loop
assertions.description: States that large-plan ends the bounded phase in pr-loop.
assertions.text: Follows /large-plan to /pr-loop

assertions.name: resolves-owner-to-agent-routing
assertions.description: Resolves pre-PR reviewer and pane ownership to agent-routing Review routing.
assertions.text: Names /agent-routing § Review routing as the owner

assertions.name: does-not-claim-large-plan-restates-routing
assertions.description: Does not claim that large-plan itself defines who opens or performs pair review.
assertions.text: Does NOT locate reviewer-routing prose in /large-plan
